subject: Architecture
title: The Silver Bridge Collapse: Hidden Corrosion
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Silver Bridge Collapse: Hidden Corrosion usable.

hook.text: On December 15, 1967, a West Virginia bridge collapsed during rush hour, killing 46 people.

buildup.text: The Silver Bridge used eyebar chains instead of wire cables — a single link failure could doom the span.

discovery.text: A tiny 0.1-inch crack in one eyebar grew undetected over decades until the chain snapped under load.

twist.text: Congress responded by creating the National Bridge Inspection Standards — mandatory checks for every U.S. bridge.

climax.text: Today, every bridge in America is inspected at least every two years. The Silver Bridge made it law.

punchline.text: Forty-six people died from a crack the size of a grain of sand.

quiz.question: What law resulted from the Silver Bridge collapse?
options: A ban on eyebar chain bridges nationwide
Mandatory bridge inspections every two years for all U.S. bridges
Required seismic retrofitting of all suspension bridges
